answer: Only weakly, and not consistently. On 29,091 inspected structures (16,244 destroyed vs 14,155 not destroyed overall; uninspected and Inaccessible excluded), an equal-weight composite using the pre-set directions (tight spacing, high density, steep slope, near open land) gives pooled AUC 0.526 (bootstrap 95% 0.519-0.533), barely above chance. It splits by fire: Palisades AUC 0.68 (top-decile 82% destroyed vs bottom 31%), Eaton 0.44, below chance. Density (0.72) and spacing (0.66) carry Palisades; slope helps a little in Eaton (0.62). Open-land distance runs opposite to the stated direction in both fires (AUC 0.38 pooled): destroyed structures were farther from open land, i.e. in the dense interior. Features are not refit. Describes structures the fires reached, not where fire will spread; wind, embers, vegetation and hardening are missing.
traps_or_caveats: 14,993 footprints (33%) have no DINS record: excluded, not counted as survivors; they differ from inspected ones (e.g. median open-land distance 306 vs 420 m), so inspection is not random. 41 Inaccessible also excluded.
Selection by outcome: layer was chosen by final perimeters (reached structures only); results say nothing about where fire goes. Perimeter distance not used (outcome leakage).

Feature directions fixed from the case file, not fitted. Open-land distance contradicts its stated direction (reversing it would be post-hoc fitting); at best the reversed sign suggests it proxies urban-core location.
Pooled AUC hides opposite behaviour in the two fires (Eaton below chance); report per fire. Fires assigned by footprint centroid UTM X<380000.

AUC is on all inspected structures, not independent samples: strong spatial autocorrelation and clustering, so the bootstrap interval is too narrow; no spatial cross-validation done. Composite is equal-weight percentile rank, no model fitted.

Open land is >100 m from any footprint in the layer; distances near the layer edge are unreliable (400 m edge buffer masks them), giving ~4% missing slope/open-land values (10% in Palisades), dropped from composite.
Footprints include sheds/outbuildings (1,444 labelled <30 m2) and 2023 footprints may differ from pre-fire reality; DINS 'Destroyed' is >50% damage, not total loss. Slope from 5 m 3DEP DEM.
Wind, embers, vegetation, roof material and defensible space are not available and not estimated; Santa Ana wind-driven ember fire makes pre-fire geometry a weak ranker.
Score My Layer was not run: it pairs a prediction with a truth catalog source, and here the features come from the same joined layer as the outcome; AUCs were computed directly.
